newsitem.title: FRANCE: DHL still seeks French site for Rhine hub.
newsitem.headline: DHL still seeks French site for Rhine hub.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express said it still preferred France for the location of its disputed Rhine Valley hub, DHL Aviation business development manager, Stephen Lewis told Reuters.
DHL had planned to establish the hub in Strasbourg but this collapsed when the project was contested by residents and local authorities.

"Strasbourg was a setback but DHL remains committed to establishing a Rhine valley hub in the not-too-distant-future, given the strong traffic volumes we are achieving in the region coupled with encouraging growth forecasts," Lewis said in an interview.
The hub would serve a region encompassing Nancy, Metz and Strasbourg in France, Basle in Switzerland and Stuttgart, Mannheim and Karlsruhe in Germany.

Following the opposition to its Strasbourg project, DHL had been looking at several sites in the Alsace-Lorraine region and on the other side of the Rhine in Germany, including existing or former military airlfields as well as commercial airports, Lewis added.

"Over the past few weeks, DHL has met with French Transport and Defence ministry officials to identify potential sites which would have the backing of the state and public authorities. We are now awaiting the government's conclusions," he said.

"A Rhine Valley hub situated in France continues to be our first choice as it is our strategy to pursue investment opportunities for operational facilities in several different countries. For example, in Germany, we already have three sub-hubs, at Frankfurt, Cologne and Nuremberg. It would also help galvanise DHL's already-buoyant activties in France."

During question time in the French parliament last week, Defence minister, Charles Millon, said the ministry is willing to study a DHL operation at the Toul-Rosieres airbase in Lorraine. This is due to close in summer 1998 as part of France's armed forces rationalisation programme.

A "significant number" of French provincial airports contacted DHL offering their facilties as a Rhine Valley hub in place of Strasbourg airport, including Metz-Nancy-Lorraine airport, situated 110 kilometres to the north-west o.

"Frankly, Metz-Nancy is too far west to be an ideal location, while Toul-Rosieres would not appear to be any better-placed. However, we don't want to exclude any of the sites under consideration at this stage."
Lewis added there was little chance Strasbourg would re-emerge as a potential location.

"It's very unlikely that Strasbourg airport's environment committee will come back to us with fresh proposals especially when one takes into account the support there appears to be for a night-time ban on flights."
DHL had planned to start at Strasbourg airport with one or two nightly flights using Convair and Electra aircraft, in the during the last quarter of 1996 rising to seven flights nightly in 1997.
The flights would have linked Strabsourg with its European hub at Brussels and express company's regional hubs.

In an initial three to four year phase of operation, DHL had outlined plans to invest US$5 million at the site creating 350 jobs. Long-term plans centred on a move into a US$50 million purpose-built facility around the turn of the century as traffic volumes increased.
